holding_summary: Stockholders who furnished supplies to a corporation's farm tenants were not entitled to a landlord's lien because the lien benefits only the landlord (the corporation itself); a prior-recorded crop mortgage with a general description was upheld as valid against a later mortgagee.
notes: Landlord's lien priority and crop-mortgage description dispute on farm rental land; no dwelling/room letting issue.

holding_summary: A homestead purchased by a married minor for himself and his family was a 'necessary' for which he was liable, and the trial court's definition of necessaries was not erroneous for failing to separately address renting versus buying or a speculative purpose.
notes: Necessaries-doctrine case for a minor's home purchase; mentions renting the house out and a precedent about a rooming-house leasehold only in passing, not as an adjudicated letting issue.

holding_summary: A landlord who did not participate in her co-defendants' unauthorized entry onto leased farmland was entitled to be sued in her home county rather than the county of the trespass, and the wrongful-dispossession damages charge was remanded for error.
notes: Venue and damages dispute over wrongful dispossession of a farm lessee; agricultural land, not dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: The court upheld a deed by which an abandoned wife, in necessitous circumstances, conveyed community property without her husband's joinder, finding her authorized to sell as a feme sole; her livelihood running the family home as a rooming and boarding house was cited as part of the necessity showing.

quotes.text: witness managed and controlled the property in controversy and made a living for herself and three children, with the aid of the older boy, by using the premises as a rooming and boarding house
she managed and controlled the property in controversy and made a living for herself and children, with the aid of the oldest son, by taking boarders and roomers

was vested with the right and authority to make conveyance of the property in question, as a feme sole, and that, her deed and her acknowledgment thereto being in regular form and legal, the conveyance of said property to defendant, Hicks, was valid any binding and passed the entire title

notes: The householder's running of the family dwelling as a rooming/boarding house is treated as an ordinary, unquestioned means of livelihood supporting the necessity finding, but the court never characterizes the legal nature of that letting arrangement (lease/license/lodging), so characterization is left null.

holding_summary: An 18-year-old who entered a company's employee shower bath house without permission for his own pleasure was at most a bare licensee owed no duty to keep the premises safe, so a directed verdict for the company was proper.
notes: Attractive-nuisance/licensee premises-liability case at an employer's bath house; unrelated to dwelling or room letting.

holding_summary: A lessor who sold leased commercial property (a horse/mule barn) before the lease term ended was individually liable, under the lease's own terms, to repay the tenants' rent deposit to the tenants' assignee, notwithstanding the tenants' failure to formally surrender possession within 90 days.
notes: Commercial-building lease deposit dispute; not dwelling/room letting by a householder.

holding_summary: Commercial lessees forfeited their building lease under the anti-subletting statute by letting sub-tenants occupy part of the premises with their consent, even though the arrangement was accommodative, uncompensated, and conditioned on the landlord's approval.
notes: Subletting-forfeiture dispute over commercial office space; not dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: A brewing company's threat not to renew saloon leases unless tenants stopped selling a competitor's beer was a lawful exercise of its rights as landlord over its own leased premises and did not violate the antitrust laws or common law.
notes: Antitrust/boycott dispute over saloon lease restrictions; commercial leasing, not dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: Where co-owners' oil and gas lease used language implying fee ownership, title to an undivided interest later acquired by the lessor from her children passed by estoppel to the lessee, validating the lease as to that interest.
notes: After-acquired-title estoppel dispute over an oil and gas mineral lease; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: A Dallas ordinance confining bawdy houses to a designated district was upheld as a valid exercise of the police power that neither conflicted with the state's criminal prohibition on bawdy houses nor unconstitutionally damaged nearby property without compensation.
notes: Concerns municipal zoning/confinement of bawdy (prostitution) houses under the police power, a distinct vice-regulation category from licensing of ordinary lodging or boarding houses; outside the corpus's short-term letting scope.

holding_summary: An employee of a commissary the railroad permitted to operate on its depot grounds was more than a bare licensee while on the grounds for purposes connected to his employment, so a general demurrer to his wrongful-death suit was improperly sustained.
notes: Invitee/licensee premises-liability case at a railroad depot commissary; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: A statute criminalizing unauthorized resale of railroad tickets was held unconstitutional because it left it optional with each railroad company, via the notice printed on a ticket, whether resale of that ticket was penal—an unlawful delegation of legislative power.
notes: Railroad-ticket scalping statute case; the 'incident of ownership' language matched by the selector concerns ticket property rights, not dwelling letting.

holding_summary: A city ordinance confining tenpin (bowling) alleys to a remote, impractical location was an unreasonable exercise of the regulatory power because it effectively prohibited rather than merely regulated the business, and was therefore void.
notes: Municipal regulation of tenpin-alley location; unrelated to dwelling or room letting.

holding_summary: A conviction for keeping a disorderly house was reversed because the evidence showed only that the defendant occupied one room by sufferance and exercised some supervision, not that she was the owner, lessee, or tenant of the house as the statute requires.
notes: Concerns criminal liability for keeping a disorderly (prostitution) house and the owner/lessee/tenant element of that offense, not licensing of lodging/boarding houses or ordinary compensated occupancy.

holding_summary: A city ordinance establishing a hack stand near a train depot was a reasonable exercise of the police power, but the provision requiring only hack and omnibus drivers (not street-car conductors) to remain with their vehicles while soliciting patronage was an unlawful discrimination rendering the ordinance void.
notes: Municipal regulation of hack/omnibus stands and solicitation at a depot; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: In a murder prosecution arising from resistance to an officer re-executing a writ of possession on leased farmland, the court held the writ was not functus officio and remanded for charge error regarding when a coconspirator's declarations could be considered.
notes: Murder/conspiracy case arising from a farmland-eviction dispute; agricultural tenancy, not dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: The private-residence exception to the gaming statute for an ordinary head-to-head dice game does not extend to an exhibitor operating a banking (table) game, so a defendant who ran a craps bank at his residence was properly convicted of exhibiting a banking game.
notes: Gaming-statute prosecution turning on a private-residence exception for dice games; unrelated to dwelling letting for pay.

holding_summary: A dugout used only occasionally for cooking, sleeping, or as a storm shelter in connection with a private residence was nonetheless an 'outhouse' within the gaming statute, so a conviction for playing cards there was upheld.
notes: Gaming-statute case about whether a dugout counted as an outhouse versus part of a private residence; unrelated to dwelling/room letting for pay.
